[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical model of oligopolistic competition with heterogeneous firms and minimum wage shocks (e.g., Berger, Herkenhoff, & Mongey, 2022, 'Minimum Wages and Low-Wage Labor Markets' or similar work in the AER or QJE). — Provides a formal mechanism linking employer concentration to pass-through, generating predictions about the gap between individual and industry wage estimates. Refuting or confirming the hypothesis requires a model that can be calibrated to U.S. data.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of minimum wage pass-through studies (e.g., Allegretto & Reich, 2018; Renkin, Montialoux, & Siegenthaler, 2022) and meta-analyses of employer concentration effects on wage-price dynamics (e.g., Azar, Marinescu, & Steinbaum, 2022). — Synthesizes existing evidence on whether firm-level pass-through varies by market structure and whether individual-level earnings estimates (which account for price increases) are systematically smaller than industry-level estimates in low-concentration markets, providing corroboration or contradiction.
